hits.problem: Fingers 3 and 2 cannot span the major sixth C3-A3; the same chord is taken 5+1 just before and after.
Finger 3 is assigned to both A2 and E3 of one chord; the thumb should keep E3 from the octave before.
Thumb on Eb5 between two E5s, then 5 lands a semitone above it at sixteenth speed: cramped, and thumb on a black key.
Rising C#5-Eb5-E5 fingered 5-4-3: 5 takes C#5 while still holding E5, then 4 and 3 land above the held 5.

Finger 3 on both C5 and E5 of the third; continue the 1-3, 2-4 sequence with 3-5.

Rising G4 to Bb4 with 3 then 2 makes the index cross over the middle finger, or forces a jump.

Fingers 2 and 3 cannot hold the minor sixth A3-F4 together.
Finger 3 plays G5 and then F5 straight after the sixteenth, breaking the descending line.

Shifting 2-3-4 across the repeated A5s walks the hand for nothing; the F5-C6 five-finger position, 5-4-3-3-3-2-1, needs no shift.
Repeated F5 quarters fingered 2-1-2 swap fingers back and forth for no gain at this tempo; keep the thumb.
The thumb must play D5 while still holding the dotted-half Bb4, and then hops from D5 to Eb5.
The A2 octave takes 4+1 here but 5+1 at L19 and L23; in this all-white bar keep 5 throughout.
Thumb plays E4 then D4 in the falling upper line; with 5 holding G3, 1-2-3-4 keeps the line legato.
Same thumb hop E4 to D4 in the repeated figure; use 1-2-3-4 over the G3 pedal as in bar 13.

The same Bb3+D4 third is 3+1 here but 4+2 at its two repeats; 4+2 from the start keeps 4 on Bb3 throughout.
Fifth finger on black G#4 for the repeated tritone; 4+1 suits the tritone and leads 4 to 3 into A4.
Thumb slides from the held E4 to F4 with no rest, breaking the legato resolution into bar 23.

Eb5 held by 4 while 3 plays Bb4 below: a perfect fourth between 3 and 4, beyond their third limit.
A3 on 3 leaves 3 and 5 on adjacent keys G3-A3; in this G five-finger position A3 naturally takes 4.
Opening turn G3-F3-G3 (and F3-E3-F3) on weak 4-5-4, then G3 is re-fingered 3; 3-4-3 keeps one octave position all bar.
4-1 on B3-E4 forces the hand up a step at C#4; 5-2 sets the B3-F#4 five-finger position held through L7.
2+5 on the third C5-E5 cramps the hand and differs from the 1+3 and 3+5 thirds used at R12-R17.
Re-striking G#4 with the thumb puts it on a black key for a half note; keeping 2 is simpler for a student.
1-4 octaves on C# are good legato technique but a stretch for a medium hand; a student can play them 1-5.
Re-fingering E3+G#3+D4 from 5+3+1 to 5+4+2+1 one eighth later shifts the hand; take it 5+4+2 from the start.

Here 5 takes G3 (F3 in bar 20) although 4 does elsewhere, so 5 shuffles across three keys; 4 keeps the octave position.

G4 is a half note on 5, yet 3 plays G#4 above it and 5 is reused on C5 while G4 sounds.
Finger 2 slides F4 to G4 while F4 still sounds; thumb then leaves held D4 for A4 and slides to Bb4.
Thumb moves D5 straight to black-key Eb5 between chords, breaking the legato; 2+4 then 5 connects.

4-3-2 on Bb5-G#5-Eb5 opens a full fourth between 3 and 2 at eighth speed; 5-4-2-1 sits naturally.

Thumb slides E4, D4, C4 in succession over the repeated G3, breaking the upper line; keep 5 on G3 and walk down 1-2-3-4.

Finger 2 takes D4 and then F4 around the thumb; in the C4-G4 position D4 belongs to 4.
The thumb holds E4 (whole note) when it must play D4 on beat 3; with 5 on A3 the hand keeps both.
While 3 holds G4, finger 2 must strike C4 a fifth below; 2-3 cannot span a fifth.
R17-R24 repeat R1-R8 a step higher, but 3-4-5 replaces 2-3-4, so 3 slides from Bb4 straight to A4.

The same 2-1 seesaw in bar 4; 4 on A3 and G#3, 3 on B3, 2 on C#4, 1 on D4 needs no shift.

Finger 4 plays G5 then F5 back to back in a stepwise descent; 4-3-2-1 is the natural fingering.

Octave Bb2-Bb3 on fingers 3 and 2; 2-3 reaches at most a fourth.

objections_on_fhmm3.problem: Bar 3 uses only fingers 2 and 1, relocating the hand on almost every sixteenth; all notes fit one position B3-F#4.

Identical chord C4-Eb4-G#4 on consecutive beats is fingered 3+2+1, then 4+2+1; C4 changes finger for no reason.
